about: Where the Rust port (crates/mosh) fixed the app's Swift mosh client (Moshpit/Services/Mosh/ as it was at b4b8e1b4, the sources harness/build-swift.sh compiles), and which fixes the Swift client has carried since (each fix's 'swift_fix' names its commit; 'swift' and 'swift_before' describe b4b8e1b4). Each fix is marked 'Fix (<id>)' in the Rust source. Both implementations now print the same for every input harness/equivalence.py feeds them (fuzz, recorded mosh-server sessions, real zlib streams and hand-built code sets, SSP scenarios with redraws, timestamps, idle steps and input split into chained instructions), except on the fixtures of the one fix still open in Swift ('status': 'open'). Wire-level fixes have a minimal case in tests/fixtures/wire/divergences.txt: divergences.rust.txt is what Rust prints for it, divergences.swift.txt what the Swift client prints now, divergences.swift-b4b8e1b4.txt what it printed before the fixes (every line differs from Rust's). 'severity' is the user-visible impact of the Swift behaviour before the fix. 'notes' are differences that remain, with their reason.

fixes.swift: MoshTransport.swift:508-511 (flush builds TransportInstruction() and never sets throwawayNum)
fixes.symptom: After 1024 user states in one session (keystroke batches and resizes), every keystroke takes up to 15 s to reach the remote shell, for the rest of the session. mosh-server keeps a received user state until the client's throwaway_num passes it; with 0 nothing is ever dropped, and past 1024 states (networktransport-impl.h, Transport::recv) the server accepts one new state per 15 s and silently drops the rest.
fixes.trigger: Type 1025 keys (one state each) in one mosh session, then type again.
fixes.minimal_input: harness/live.py throwaway: 1100 single keys 15 ms apart against mosh-server 1.4.0
fixes.swift_before: key #1025 reached the remote 15060 ms after it was typed; 76 keys over 1 s; p99 14882 ms
fixes.swift_after: p99 1 ms, max 16 ms over the same 1100 keys (live)
fixes.fix: Every instruction carries throwaway_num = the acked user state (the oldest state the client still diffs from), as mosh's own client does (transportsender-impl.h: sent_states.front().num).
fixes.rust_outcome: max 2 ms, p99 1 ms over the same 1100 keys
evidence: harness/equivalence.py: every scenario checks thr=old on both sides
fixes.severity: high: matches the field report that typing over mosh dies after a while (2026-08-17)
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): tell mosh-server which user states it may throw away

fixes.symptom: mosh-server crashes (SIGSEGV in Network::UserStream::diff_from, from Transport::get_remote_diff) and takes the remote shell with it; on builds with asserts it aborts. Swift strips expired keystrokes out of states it already sent. When the server did receive them and only its acks were lost, the next user state no longer extends the one the server processed; mosh-server compares user streams by position, so it drops as many new events as were stripped, or reads past the end of the shorter state.
fixes.trigger: The return path drops packets for more than the 10 s keystroke TTL after something was typed (the forward path working), then the user types again.
fixes.minimal_input: harness/live.py ttl: type 'abcde', drop server-to-client datagrams from 1.9 s to 16 s, type 'x' at 14 s and 'yz' at 18 s
fixes.swift_before: the remote read 'abcde' only; mosh-server died (crash report: EXC_BAD_ACCESS in UserStream::diff_from)
fixes.swift_after: the remote read 'abcdexyz' ('x' 3684 ms after it was typed, once the path healed); server alive (live)
fixes.fix: Keystrokes past the TTL are dropped at once only from states never sent. When a sent one expires, flushes carry no user state past the acked one (still acking host states) until the server answers: an ack covering the sent states means they arrived and nothing is dropped; a datagram arriving 5 s or more into the hold, with them still unacked, means they never did, and only then are the expired keystrokes dropped. No state the server may hold is ever rewritten.
fixes.rust_outcome: the remote read 'abcdexyz' ('x' 3.9 s after it was typed, when the path healed); server alive
fixes.severity: high: kills the session; also input typed blind into a dead return path is mangled
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): never rewrite user states mosh-server may already hold

fixes.swift: MoshTransport.swift:309-316 (requestFullRedraw: both resizes in one user state)
fixes.symptom: requestFullRedraw (the diagnostics popover's repaint, and every forced resume after more than 20 s in the background) never repaints. mosh-server applies both resizes before it renders, sees no size change and sends nothing; cells the client got wrong are never resent.
fixes.minimal_input: harness/live.py redraw: a static 22-line screen, then requestFullRedraw
fixes.swift_after: 1715 bytes: ESC[r ESC[0m ESC[H ESC[2J and all 22 lines, the same bytes as the Rust client (live)
fixes.fix: The narrower width goes alone; the frame the server renders at it is applied and acked but not shown; then the real width, whose frame is a complete repaint. Frames in between are hidden for at most 5 s; a real resize cancels the redraw.
fixes.rust_outcome: 1715 bytes: ESC[r ESC[0m ESC[H ESC[2J and all 22 lines
fixes.severity: medium: the documented self-heal for the white-block render divergence does nothing
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): a requested redraw makes mosh-server repaint the screen

fixes.swift: MoshTransport.swift:672-678 (updateSRTT treats reply 0 as none), 680-684 (outgoingTimestampReply sends 0, then the same saved timestamp forever), 610-611 (reordered datagrams update both), 727-729 (timestamp16 can read 0xFFFF)
fixes.symptom: The SRTT shown in the terminal pill jumps to bogus values for about 5 s every 65.5 s: the server marks 'nothing to echo' with 0xFFFF, which Swift takes as an RTT sample of now16 + 1 ms whenever the low 16 bits of its clock are under 5000. A reordered or replayed datagram also feeds an old echo in. Toward the server, the first replies are 0, a bogus first sample for mosh-server's own SRTT (and so its frame interval) 7.6% of the time.
fixes.trigger: Normal operation: any server datagram sent without a fresh client timestamp to echo (bursts of output, idle acks).
fixes.swift_before: SRTT sample of 1001 ms from a 0xFFFF reply at clock 3*65536+1000
fixes.fix: mosh network.cc rules: 0xFFFF means no timestamp both ways and our clock skips it; an echo goes out once, advanced by the time held, only within 1 s; datagrams older than one already seen feed neither RTT nor echo; the first sample seeds SRTT whatever its value.
evidence: tests/transport_fixes.rs: a_no_timestamp_reply_is_not_a_sample, a_zero_first_sample_seeds_the_estimate, an_older_datagram_feeds_no_timestamps, the_echo_is_fresh_and_used_once, our_timestamp_never_reads_as_missing, a_fragmented_flush_echoes_once
fixes.severity: low: display only on the client
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): read 0xFFFF, not 0, as mosh's "no timestamp"

fixes.swift: MoshCompression.swift:31-37 (decompress strips 2 + 4 bytes unchecked and raw-inflates the rest with Apple's COMPRESSION_ZLIB decoder)
fixes.symptom: A stream with a wrong zlib header or Adler-32 trailer inflates anyway (RFC 1950 requires a decompressor to check both; mosh's own client does, via zlib uncompress), and Apple's DEFLATE decoder also accepts a stored block whose NLEN is not the complement of LEN and an invalid code-length set, both of which zlib rejects. Datagrams are authenticated, so only a broken server could send one.
fixes.trigger: Any zlib stream whose header check bits or trailer are wrong but whose DEFLATE body inflates, or a body with the two DEFLATE faults above.
fixes.swift_after: err badChecksum / badHeader / inflateFailed, the real zlib's verdict on every zlib.decompress case
fixes.fix: Header (FCHECK, method 8, window <= 32 KiB, no preset dictionary), DEFLATE (by zlib's rules, src/inflate.rs) and Adler-32 are all checked; inflation stops at mosh's 4 MiB buffer. Every such difference in fuzzing is confirmed against the real zlib, which rejects the input too, and on every zlib.decompress case Rust's result equals zlib's. The Swift client inflates with the system zlib (raw DEFLATE after its own header check, then the Adler-32 that follows the DEFLATE stream), so it gives exactly the real zlib's verdict. The Rust port inflated with miniz_oxide until "fix(mosh): the Rust port inflates by zlib's rules, not miniz_oxide's" (src/inflate.rs): miniz_oxide also accepted a literal/length or distance code set of a single code longer than one bit, which zlib refuses, and took such a stream as valid when its Adler-32 matched (5,589 of 200,000 differential cases against the real zlib gave another verdict, most of them accepted; 0 now).
evidence: harness/equivalence.py check_against_real_zlib(): both sides give the real zlib's verdict, on the fuzz and on code_set_cases() (a single code of every length, both alphabets, and random small sets)
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): inflate server instructions as strictly as zlib's uncompress

fixes.swift: MoshBootstrap.swift:190-193 (first match of pid\s*=\s*(\d+) anywhere in the output)
fixes.symptom: The session later runs `kill <pid>` on the user's host to reap a mosh-server that never heard from the client. The pid is the first 'pid = N' anywhere in the exec output, so a shell startup file printing e.g. 'rapid = 5' before mosh-server's line names an unrelated process; 'pid = 0' would make it `kill 0`, the whole process group.
fixes.trigger: Output before the detach line containing lower-case 'pid' then '=' then digits; or a detach line with pid 0.
fixes.fix: Only mosh-server's '[mosh-server detached, pid = N]' line counts, matched on bytes, and pids 0 and 1 are refused (a forked server is never either), matching the comment's intent ('reaping is then skipped, never guessed'). The Rust parser refused only 0 until the Swift fix; both refuse 1 now.
evidence: harness/equivalence.py: generated bootstrap output with pid-like banners and pids 0 and 1
fixes.severity: low likelihood, high consequence (kills an unrelated user process)
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): reap only the pid mosh-server's detach line names, never 0 or 1

fixes.symptom: The connect line's prefix and field separators are matched by grapheme cluster: a combining mark right after a space glues it to the next field, so that line is skipped or misparsed.
fixes.trigger: A combining character right after 'MOSH CONNECT ' or between fields.
fixes.swift_before: the glued line is skipped; a later connect line wins
fixes.swift_after: err noConnectLine on the glued line
fixes.fix: Matched on bytes, as mosh-server writes them (same decision as the tmux crate's unicode-syntax fix).
fixes.rust_outcome: err noConnectLine on the glued line
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): match the MOSH CONNECT line by scalar, not by Character

fixes.symptom: A resize varint outside 32 bits keeps all 64; protobuf (and mosh-server's parser) cut int32 to its low 32 bits. The client never uses a decoded resize.
fixes.trigger: A ResizeMessage width or height varint >= 2^31.
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): decode resize width and height as int32

fixes.symptom: Display only. Swift counts 100 grapheme clusters and also escapes every unassigned code point of planes 0-3 and 14 in Foundation's tables (CharacterSet.illegalCharacters; 138,502 code points on macOS 27) while keeping the noncharacters of planes 4-16.
fixes.trigger: Non-ASCII remote output in an error message.
fixes.swift_before: U+0378 escaped, U+4FFFE kept; 'e' + U+0301 counted as one
fixes.fix: 100 scalars (CRLF as one); escapes C0/C1, Cf, default-ignorables and all noncharacters; no Unicode-version table. Identical on ASCII and on every assigned code point.
fixes.rust_outcome: U+0378 kept, U+4FFFE escaped; the combining mark cut at the 100th unit
fixes.open_because: Display only (an error message excerpt); not part of this fix round.

fixes.symptom: Fragmenting an instruction into 65,536 or more pieces traps (an 84 MB compressed instruction at the transport's MTU).
fixes.trigger: A paste that compresses to over 84 MB.
fixes.fix: Numbers keep wrapping in 15 bits like the Swift initializer masks them; mosh-server would refuse such an instruction anyway (4 MiB inflate limit).
fixes.swift_fix: fix(mosh): fragmenting a huge instruction no longer traps

notes: Compression is not byte-identical: Apple's COMPRESSION_ZLIB is zlib 1.2.12's deflate at level 5 (probed: identical output to zlib level 5, memLevel 8, for every sample), the Rust port uses miniz_oxide at level 6 behind the same 78 9C header and Adler-32. Every compressed output is checked to inflate on the other side and in the real zlib.

Not changed: the client ignores the instruction's protocol_version (mosh's client aborts on a mismatch), sends no chaff, gives each instruction a new id (mosh reuses it for a retransmission), acks a duplicate or stale diff only with its next datagram, and accepts an ack for a user state it never sent (mosh ignores those). None is observable against mosh-server.

Both clients send by mosh's sender discipline (transportsender-impl.h; fix(mosh): send by mosh's sender discipline, not a flush per frame): new input at most once per send interval (SRTT/2, 20 to 250 ms) from the state the server is assumed to hold, unacked input again once the oldest of it has gone mosh's retransmission timeout (SRTT + 4 RTTVAR, 50 ms to 1 s) plus its 100 ms ACK_DELAY without an ack, and only within 10 s of last hearing the server (ACTIVE_RETRY_TIMEOUT); output acked within ACK_DELAY; a datagram at least every 3 s (ACK_INTERVAL). Where they differ from mosh-client, by design: a retransmission restamps every state it carries (mosh restamps only the newest, so it retries every send interval until the ack comes); SEND_MINDELAY is 0 (mosh-client's 1 ms gathers one burst of reads; send() is handed whole inputs); the retry window opens with the first datagram (mosh-client's opens only once the server is heard, so its lost first datagram waits 3 s); only empty user states are made for the 3 s ack, not one per ack. Live, a 4 MB random paste: harness/live.py paste; typing under 5% loss: harness/live.py typing.

Not changed: client-to-server fragments are up to 1300 bytes (datagrams of 1328 bytes); mosh uses a 1280-byte IPv4/IPv6 MTU. Over a 1280-MTU tunnel (Tailscale) a large paste's datagrams are fragmented by IP.
